assumptions: The 'exception detail screen' maps to the operator-console review cards (operator_console.py) and the packet detail page (packet_page.py) built by scripts/run_dogfood_pilot.py; no file literally named 'exception detail' exists.
The authoritative backend state for AC3 is workflow_runs.state in the workflow SQLite DB, read live via WorkflowStore.get_run.
test_review.py and test_dogfood_pilot.py are the existing homes for render/console coverage; the builder's new tests (if any) most plausibly live there.
The driver_probe workflow.sqlite3 is a valid workflow DB with a workflow_runs table and is safe to query read-only.

The described diff (exception_detail_view.py, exception_detail.html, workflow_store.py, authorization.py, schema.py) is present in the harness run environment; it is NOT in this checkout, so route paths and exact rendered strings could not be read from source.

Scenarios S8/S9 assume the exception detail screen is served over HTTP at http://127.0.0.1:8001 under a path like /exceptions/<id>. If it is served under a different path (or rendered as a static file rather than an HTTP route), the run harness should substitute the real route; a 404 for an unknown/bad id is the expected refusal either way.

WorkflowState literals used in forbidden_observations (NEEDS_REVIEW, RECEIVED, READY_FOR_ENTRY, DONE) are the canonical enum values from workflow.py and are what a fabricated-state leak would most plausibly emit.

No approved command can create exceptions, other-tenant rows, or unresolvable-owner fixtures, and callback POSTs require valid signatures, so scenarios needing bespoke seeded state or a known existing run_id could not be authored reliably.
unresolved_questions: No builder diff was provided; scenarios were inferred from the current render surfaces (operator_console.py, packet_page.py, review.py) and the pilot build wiring — the actual change set for U-UI-11 is unknown.

The exception detail screen is a static HTML artifact (build_operator_console / build_packet_site), not served by the app at 127.0.0.1:8001 (the callback server) and not readable via any approved command; with no browser available, screen text cannot be observed directly, so all scenarios fall back to render unit tests. Is a live/served version of this screen in scope?

AC1 'who owns it': the current render surfaces show action labels and consequences but no accountable-owner name. Was an owner field added? If not, AC1 is unmet and cannot be satisfied by the existing render code.

Which test module (if any) the builder added to cover U-UI-11 is unknown; if a dedicated operator-console/packet-page test was added, its path should be substituted into the pytest scenarios to make the observations AC-specific rather than suite-level pass/fail.

AC3 can only be indirectly verified here: I can confirm the backend authority (workflow_runs.state) and that the render sources it live in code, but without reading the generated HTML I cannot prove the rendered artifact matches after a post-build state transition.

What is the actual HTTP route (and method) for the exception detail screen, and is it served by the `callback` service on 8001 or produced as a static artifact? Exact route is needed to make screen-content scenarios reliably executable.

AC1 ('names the next action and who owns it'): authorization.py added ~88 lines of ownership logic, but with no fixture-creation command and no readable source I could not verify (a) an owner is always named, (b) an unresolvable owner is flagged rather than silently omitted (unowned_obligation/accountable_owner), or (c) cross-tenant ownership is not leaked. These need a seeded exception with a known id and tenant.

AC2 ('shows the evidence the exception was raised from'): the exact emitted evidence text/URL on the exception detail screen is unknown. review.py builds evidence links as http://localhost:8000/evidence/<load_id>/<doc_type>, but whether the exception screen reuses that format is unconfirmed, so a literal evidence assertion could not be grounded.

Does the exception detail screen offer/suppress a 'next action' for runs in TERMINAL_STATES (DONE/FAILED)? Verifying that a resolved exception is not presented as actionable requires a known terminal-state run_id, which is not obtainable with the approved commands.
